analysis.title: Blueback (George Saravelos, Deutsche Bank FX Research): market impact of the US mid-term elections
key_insights: Deutsche Bank reads the mid-term outcome as risk positive. It agrees with the overnight rebound in global equities and risky FX currencies.
A large Democratic majority in Congress plus Trump's stated willingness to work with the opposition should act as a brake on extreme policy outcomes and lower risk premia.
The market is increasingly likely to treat surprising Executive policy shifts as time-bound by the next Presidential election or the new domestic political configuration.

On Iran, Trump said in the last 48 hours that no attack is imminent and acknowledged the Iran war drove part of the election outcome. DB argues oil flows through the Middle East have materially recovered, so the market is pricing a large imminent risk premium for re-escalation and energy supply disruption.
DB sees negative time decay on the oil price: the longer escalation is delayed, the bigger the downward pressure on oil.
The largest remaining source of US domestic policy uncertainty is the debt ceiling, which becomes binding by Q2 of next year.

Republicans reportedly aim to pass a debt ceiling increase via reconciliation over the next few weeks. Success would remove a layer of fiscal uncertainty and keep AI and other policy matters from being bundled into a protracted negotiation with a Democratic Congress.
Question marks around the AI build-out are expected to persist regardless of the debt ceiling outcome.

DB's net call is that the political developments support a continued bottoming in EUR/USD, since lower energy and global policy risk premia and higher AI implementation risks should weaken the dollar.
If Congress fails to pass a debt ceiling increase this year, DB would treat it as an added dollar negative.
